spike_verdict: The core tension (a self-described steward charges $30-$40 and bars walk-ons, then was challenged in 2021 over its own founding deed) is carried by the evidence, but the spike_statement overstates two specifics beyond what the sheet supports: it says the club 'faced a lawsuit' when the sheet's own spike_candidate and F26 describe only a retained attorney pursuing a claim (no filing, no outcome, ever documented), and it applies 'since 1952' to the $30-$40 price and walk-on ban, which are sourced only to the current (2026) site, not to 1952.

blocking.problem: No source documents a filed lawsuit. F26 (Newport Buzz, 2021) says Brooke Richter 'retained... attorney Amy Rice to represent her in a quest to make Gooseberry essentially a public beach' — an attorney was retained, not litigation filed. The fact sheet's own spike_candidate hedges this correctly as a 'lawsuit threat.' The rest of the page (history.mdx, overview.mdx) correctly say 'retained an attorney,' 'legal action,' 'legal threat' — only the SPIKE headline claim inflates this to 'a lawsuit,' which is a service-level overstatement (the exact 'announced'→'built' class this audit flags).

blocking.fix: Rescope "since 1952" to modify only the shareholder-run status, e.g.: "A shareholder club, running the beach since 1952, now charges $30-$40 a day and bans walk-ons — then in 2021 faced a legal threat over the deed it cites as proof of access."

blocking.claim: "Gooseberry Beach sits on land that has generated at least two serious disputes over who gets to use it — one in 1880, one in 2021, more than a century apart — over the same underlying question: what does ownership of this stretch of Newport coastline actually entitle the public to?"
blocking.problem: The 1880 event (F08, F09) is a contested will/probate dispute over inheritance of the Hazard estate — the sheet gives no indication it was a dispute over public access or beach use. Framing it as the same kind of dispute as the 2021 public-access fight, and as being about 'who gets to use it,' recasts a family/estate contest as an access-rights dispute the sheet does not support.
blocking.evidence: F08: "upon his death in 1880, his will was the subject of contention and controversy." F09: the contested estate "resulted in the gift of rocky farm to the newport hospital." Neither mentions public access, beach use, or a rival claimant to use of the shore.
blocking.fix: Reframe to avoid equating the two: e.g. "Gooseberry Beach sits on land shaped by two separate disputes a century apart: an 1880 fight over Hazard's estate that determined who would own this stretch of coastline, and a 2021 fight over what the public is entitled to once inside that ownership." Or delete the false-equivalence framing entirely and let the two events stand on their own timeline.
